tax.text: Day says he would keep taxes low for working families and cut wasteful government spending.
tax.quote:
Cut wasteful government spending
Keep taxes low for working families
Simplify the tax system
Increase transparency and accountability

wages.text: In an interview, Day identified raising the minimum wage as one of the priorities he would fight for in Congress.
wages.quote: Asked what he would actually fight for in Congress, Day pointed to traditional Democratic priorities like raising the minimum wage

debt.text: Day says he would defend Social Security and Medicare benefits and make no cuts to earned benefits.
debt.quote:
Defend Social Security and Medicare benefits
No cuts to earned benefits
Strengthen programs for long-term stability

safety.text: Day calls for cracking down on violent crime, stopping fentanyl trafficking, and supporting police and first responders.
safety.quote:
Crack down on violent crime
Stop fentanyl trafficking and distribution
Support police and first responders

immigration.text: His platform combines border enforcement with a call for clear legal immigration pathways.
immigration.quote:
Enforce the law and secure the border
Stop illegal trafficking and fentanyl at the source
Fix a broken system with clear, legal pathways

abortion.text: Day says he would defend bodily autonomy and the right to make personal medical decisions.
abortion.quote: Government should not control your body, your healthcare, or your personal life.

energy.text: Day supports Louisiana oil and gas jobs and an all-of-the-above energy strategy that includes renewables to lower costs.
energy.quote: It also means an all-of-the-above energy strategy — supporting the oil and gas jobs that power our economy and investing in renewable energy to lower costs, strengthen our grid, and secure our future.

tax.text: She proposes higher taxes on top earners and large fortunes to help fund expanded health coverage and other programs.
tax.quote: An income tax increase on high earners, the top 1 percent, to ensure that the wealthy pay their fair share.

wages.text: She criticized the federal minimum wage as insufficient for families to live with dignity.
wages.quote: It is deeply concerning to expect hardworking people and families to survive on just $7.25 an hour, the federal minimum wage.

trade.text: She supports free trade with Canada and further trade agreements with labor and environmental protections.
trade.quote: We should pursue a free trade policy with Canada on goods and services to ensure that we are able to grow both our economies and hold a strong relationship between Americans and Canadians.

debt.text: She says she would protect Social Security and Medicare from cuts and expand benefits.
debt.quote: Protect Social Security and Medicare from cuts, and expand benefits to ensure that seniors can retire with security.

housing.text: She supports zoning reforms that reduce restrictions and allow higher-density housing.
housing.quote: This includes advocating for policies that reduce zoning restrictions, allow for higher density housing, and promote mixed-use developments.

schools.text: She strongly opposes school-choice programs and says they harm lower-income children.
schools.quote: School choice is only to benefit the wealthy and harms our children of lower income.

safety.text: She supports crisis teams and treatment as alternatives to relying on law enforcement for behavioral health and addiction crises.
safety.quote: We cannot arrest our way out of a public health crisis. We must treat addiction as a disease, not a crime and invest in treatment, recovery and prevention.

immigration.text: She supports comprehensive immigration reform that includes a pathway to citizenship and addressing the causes of migration.
immigration.quote: I support comprehensive immigration reform that includes a pathway to citizenship and addressing the root causes of migration.

guns.text: She supports universal background checks and what she calls common-sense gun reform.
guns.quote: What restrictions on gun ownership are needed to protect public safety? Universal background checks and common-sense gun reform .

abortion.text: She says she would codify abortion rights, repeal the Hyde Amendment, and expand access to reproductive health care.
abortion.quote: Codify Roe v. Wade into federal law, protecting the right to abortion in every state.

gender.text: She strongly disagrees with barring transgender women and girls from women’s sports and sex-segregated spaces.
gender.quote:
Biological males should not be allowed to participate in women's sports or occupy biological women's spaces whether it be bathrooms, locker rooms, sorority houses, women's shelters, or prison.

Strongly Disagree

health.text: She proposes a single public insurance program covering all Americans through a Medicare for All plan.
health.quote: Every American would be automatically enrolled in a single, public insurance program.

energy.text: She strongly agrees that human-caused climate change requires urgent political action.
energy.quote:
Man-made climate change is a global threat and requires urgent political action.

Strongly Agree

voting.text: She strongly agrees that people should be able to vote without photo identification.
voting.quote:
People should be able to vote without photo identification.

Strongly Agree

tax.text: He supported the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and says he will continue to support lower taxes.
tax.quote: As your Congressman, I will continue to support lower taxes and push back against any effort to raise taxes on hardworking American families.

wages.text: He voted against the Raise the Wage Act.
wages.quote:
Vote Question: On Passage

Raise the Wage Act

Vote Type: Recorded Vote

trade.text: He supported tariffs on imported seafood and rice to protect domestic producers.
trade.quote: I support President Trump’s efforts to level the playing field and protect America’s domestic industry.

debt.text: He backed and advocated for the Social Security Fairness Act, which repealed provisions that reduced some public workers’ benefits.
debt.quote: Congressman Higgins has advocated for this legislation for seven years.

safety.text: He opposed reducing police funding and argued that police departments need more resources.
safety.quote: Slashing law enforcement funding injures public safety and endangers our communities.

immigration.text: He says people entering the country must follow U.S. laws and has supported legislation targeting sanctuary-city policies.
immigration.quote: In Congress, I will continue to ensure those seeking our treasures do so legally, responsibly, and with our values in their heart.

guns.text: He introduced legislation to strengthen gun-owner protections and voted against bills imposing new restrictions on firearm purchases.
guns.quote: The bill strengthens Second Amendment protections and eliminates federal barriers for law-abiding gun owners.

abortion.text: He describes himself as pro-life and has supported legislation restricting abortion and abortion funding.
abortion.quote: I believe strongly that we should do all we can as a society to protect the sanctity of life, which unquestionably begins at conception.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: He voted for legislation preventing biological males from competing in women’s sports.
gender.quote: This bill affirms Title IX’s original intent and protects women’s sports from the left’s radical gender ideology.

health.text: He supports marketplace competition and private health-insurance choices, while also saying Medicare should be protected.
health.quote: I will support legislation that encourages marketplace competition so that every Louisianan has access to affordable health insurance options.

energy.text: He supports fossil-fuel development and argues that federal energy policies can destroy jobs and raise energy costs.
energy.quote: These actions will have the same outcome now as they did then, the destruction of American jobs, higher energy costs, and undermining global security interests.

voting.text: He backed legislation requiring proof of citizenship to register and photo identification to vote.
voting.quote: legislation that would require individuals to provide documentary proof of U.S. citizenship when registering to vote and require photo identification before voting.

debt.text: LeBrun said Social Security and Medicare are necessary and that she opposes cuts to the funding beneficiaries have paid into.
debt.quote: There are improvements that should be made, but I am against any cuts to this funding that hard-working Americans have invested.

schools.text: LeBrun said public money should not go to private schools.
schools.quote: Public money should not go to private schools.

safety.text: LeBrun supported shifting funding from police and incarceration toward education, mental health care and similar services to reduce crime.
safety.quote: Do you believe the nation should reduce crime by shifting funding from police and incarceration to increased investment in education, mental healthcare, infrastructure, equitable economic opportunity, and similar systems and programs? Yes

immigration.text: Her campaign pairs targeted border enforcement with faster asylum processing, legal-status pathways, Dreamer protections, and expanded legal immigration.
immigration.quote: Create a pathway to legal status for long-term residents who pass background checks and contribute to their communities.

guns.text: LeBrun supported requiring universal background checks for firearm purchases.
guns.quote: Do you support restricting access to firearms by requiring universal background checks? Yes

abortion.text: LeBrun said abortion should be a private decision between a patient and health care provider and supported access to legal abortion.
abortion.quote: This is the private decision between a healthcare provider and their patient.

health.text: In a 2022 candidate survey, she supported Medicare for All; in another questionnaire, she selected government-funded insurance available alongside private options.
health.quote: Healthcare insurance funded by the government should be available for all who want it, along with private healthcare options.

energy.text: Her platform supports renewable and other low-carbon energy while retaining oil and gas jobs during a transition.
energy.quote: Offshore wind development where appropriate. Solar energy expansion on industrial and disturbed lands. Advanced nuclear research and deployment. Hydrogen development with strong environmental safeguards. Grid modernization and energy storage. Oil and gas jobs during a responsible energy transition.

voting.text: LeBrun agreed that people should be able to vote without photo identification and said there are other ways to verify identity.
voting.quote: There are other ways to prove who you are. Especially if the issue surrounds the state being unwilling to issue FREE photo identification to ALL citizens.
